source_contradictions: Calculated health check children: DNSLimitations row and dns-failover-determining-health-of-endpoints say 255 (route53-quota-calculated-child-health-checks, route53-hc-calculated-up-to-255-children-guide); health-checks-creating-values console text and the API reference (ChildHealthChecks array maximum, HealthThreshold maximum) say 256 (route53-hc-calculated-console-256). Use 255 as the quota; do not teach 256 as a limit.

Multivalue answer: the routing-policy-multivalue page says up to eight healthy records; best-practices-dns says it chooses eight healthy random IP addresses (route53-multivalue-recommended-eight-within-512).

Route 53 API request throttling: the throttling-api-requests page says the throttling behavior was updated (higher request rate, new change-based throttling); older material says five requests per second per account. The page gives no date; the quotas page only points to it. Account-level bucket is capacity 50, refill 10.
notes: Failure threshold default (three) and the request-interval default (30 seconds) come from the API reference page APIReference/API_HealthCheckConfig, fetched into the corpus by this miner. The failure threshold range 1 to 10 is quoted from the History page (2014 release note).

The VPC Resolver 1024 packets per second per network interface quota is quoted from the Amazon VPC quotas page (amazon-vpc-limits) and the Resolver availability page; it is route53-namespaced because it concerns the Route 53 Resolver.
